title: AECOM Design-Engineering Backlog + Insider Cluster: The Picks-and-Shovels of AI Data Centers
summary: AECOM — the world's largest infrastructure design/engineering firm — printed a record $24.8B backlog with book-to-burn above 1.0x for 18 consecutive quarters at Q2 2026, then a 3-insider cluster bought $699K near 52-week lows. Stock trades at ~$70 vs. $89 analyst target and $135 52-week high despite AI-datacenter design work becoming a growth driver.
catalyst: Q2 FY2026 earnings (May 12, 2026) disclosed record $24.8B backlog, 18 consecutive quarters of book-to-burn >1.0x, and raised full-year guidance. In the six weeks that followed (June 2026), three insiders bought common stock totaling ~$700K at prices around $70 — well below the 52-week high. Q3 FY2026 earnings (early Aug 2026) is the next dated catalyst; if book-to-burn holds and management quantifies data-center design revenue, the multi-year visibility story firms up.
thesis: ACM is a design-engineering firm, not a construction contractor — that means margin-rich planning, permitting, and engineering hours front-run construction spend by 12-24 months on data centers, water, power, and transportation. Hyperscaler capex now cycles through design firms before it ever reaches PWR/ETN. ACM has explicitly called out AI data centers as a growth driver and reports Americas Design segment as the fastest-growing part of the backlog. The insider cluster at 52-week-low prices is a meaningful vote against the market's mistrust of the margin trajectory.
counter_thesis: Margin expansion has been the persistent bear case for years and remains elusive per Barchart coverage — record backlog has not translated to record margins. Q2 revenue missed estimates by 3.6%, so book-to-burn ratios can rise while realized revenue lags. The stock's near-52-week-low print reflects real investor skepticism that ACM can convert backlog to profit at the pace larger data-center-construction pure-plays can. Design-services pricing power is also weaker than product/equipment, so hyperscaler capex tailwinds capture less economics here than at VRT or ETN. Finally, the insider buys are ~$700K — meaningful but not overwhelming for a $10B company.

ticker_rationale.ACM: World's largest infrastructure design/engineering firm. Record $24.8B backlog with book-to-burn >1.0x for 18 straight quarters. Explicit AI data-center exposure. Trading at ~$70 vs. $89 consensus target and $135 52w high; 3-insider cluster bought ~$700K in June. Screener overall score 68 (HOLD), Growth sleeve.

risks: Margin expansion continues to lag backlog growth — record orders without record profit
Revenue conversion slower than expected (Q2 missed on the top line by 3.6%)
Hyperscaler capex cyclicality — a datacenter capex pause would extend design-to-build gap materially
Design services have less pricing power than product/equipment names, capturing less of the AI infra spend

invalidation.trigger: Book-to-burn falls below 1.0x for 2 consecutive quarters
Management removes or de-emphasizes AI data-center commentary on the next 2 earnings calls
Insiders begin net selling within 90 days of this filing
